concept_definition: the uppermost or foremost part of the body of a human or animal, containing the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth
the front part of a person's head, including the forehead, eyes, nose, mouth, and chin
The organ of sight in humans and animals, typically a spherical structure containing a retina and lens that detects light and enables vision.
the part of the face above the mouth that contains the nostrils and is used for breathing and smelling
the opening and cavity in the lower part of the human face, surrounded by the lips, through which food is taken in and speech is produced
the organ on the side of the head that detects sound and helps with balance; the external part visible on humans is called the outer ear
One of the hard, calcified structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing food.
the muscular organ in the mouth used for tasting, manipulating food, and articulating speech
the part of a person or animal's body that connects the head to the rest of the body
the upper jointed part of the human body where the arm connects to the torso, including the surrounding bones, muscles, and joint
the forelimb of the human body, extending from the shoulder to the hand; the part including the upper arm, elbow, forearm, wrist, and hand
the joint between the upper and lower parts of the human arm that allows it to bend and straighten; the corresponding joint in other animals
the joint between the forearm and the hand; the part of the arm where the radius and ulna meet the carpal bones
the end part of a person's arm beyond the wrist, including the palm, fingers, and thumb
one of the long, jointed projections attached to the hand, used for feeling, grasping, and manipulating objects
the short, thick first digit on the human hand, opposable to the other fingers and used for grasping and manipulating objects
the front part of a person or animal's body between the neck and the abdomen, enclosed by the ribcage and containing the heart and lungs
the rear surface of a human or animal between the neck and the lower end of the spine; the part of the body opposite the chest
the abdominal cavity of a human or animal; the organ between the esophagus and the intestines that digests food
one of the limbs on which a person or animal stands and walks, extending from the hip to the foot
The part of the human or animal leg between the hip and the knee.
The joint between the thigh and the lower leg in humans and many animals, allowing the leg to bend and straighten; also the corresponding part on the hind limb of a quadruped.
the joint between the foot and the leg, or the region surrounding this joint
the terminal part of the leg below the ankle, on which a person stands and walks; also, the paw-like lower part of the leg of certain animals
one of the five digits at the end of the human foot, used for balance and walking
The outer protective layer of tissue covering the body of a person or animal; the epidermis and dermis collectively.
The proteinaceous strands that grow from the skin of humans and animals, typically on the head, used for protection, insulation, and appearance.
A hard, calcified connective tissue that forms the skeleton of vertebrate animals and supports and protects body organs.

A tissue in a plant or animal composed of fibers that can contract to produce movement or maintain posture; (in animals) any of the contractile organs or tissues (such as skeletal, cardiac, or smooth muscle) attached to bones or surrounding internal organs.
the muscular organ in humans and other animals that pumps blood through the circulatory system
One of the pair of organs in the chest that take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide for breathing.
The organ inside the skull that controls thought, memory, feelings, and body functions.
One of a pair of organs in the body that filter waste from the blood and produce urine.
The red fluid that circulates in the bodies of humans and animals, carrying oxygen and nutrients and removing waste.
The column of vertebrae running down the back that supports the body and protects the spinal cord; the backbone.
An internal organ in vertebrates that processes nutrients, detoxifies harmful substances, and produces bile.
The lowermost part of the human face below the mouth, forming the prominence of the jaw.
The fleshy part of the face below the eye and between the nose and the ear.
Either of the bony structures forming the upper and lower parts of the mouth, containing the teeth and enabling biting and chewing (the upper jaw = maxilla; the lower jaw = mandible).
The passage at the back of the mouth and nasal cavity that leads to the esophagus and windpipe; the front part of the neck containing the pharynx and larynx.
The hard, protective plate at the tip of a human finger.
Liquid produced by glands in the skin, often as a response to heat, exercise, or stress; perspiration.
The rear appendage of an animal's body, often long and flexible, extending from the backbone.
A limb or appendage on the body of a bird, bat, or insect, used for flying.
A drop of salty liquid produced by the eye, often as a response to emotion, irritation, or injury.
a hard, pointed growth on the head of certain animals such as cattle, goats, or rhinoceroses, made of keratin or bone
the soft tissue of a body
either of the two fleshy parts forming the edge of the mouth
the rhythmic throbbing of arteries as blood is pumped through them.
the nail on a toe.
the short, soft hair covering the skin of an animal.
the flat area formed by the upper thighs when sitting.
The projecting part on each side of the body formed by the pelvis and upper part of the thigh bone.
Any of the curved bones forming the rib cage, protecting the chest cavity and internal organs.
The part of the face above the eyebrows and below the hairline.
The strip of hair growing on the ridge above each eye socket.
The fold of skin that covers and protects the eye, able to open and close.
The part of the body between the ribs and the hips, typically the narrowest part of the torso.
The inner surface of the hand between the wrist and fingers.
The back part of the foot below the ankle.
The front part of the body below the chest, containing the stomach and other organs; the abdomen.
The bony framework of the head, enclosing and protecting the brain.
A blood vessel that carries blood toward the heart.
A bundle of fibers that transmits signals between the brain or spinal cord and other parts of the body.
A place where two or more bones meet, allowing movement and flexibility in the body.
The long tubular organ extending from the stomach to the anus, responsible for digesting food and absorbing nutrients.
one of the flat structures growing from a bird's skin, forming its plumage.
The flat part of either side of the head between the forehead and the ear.
A small dark blemish on the skin.
the bony frame enclosing the chest
the flat triangular bone of the upper back
the finger next to the thumb
the third finger, on which a ring is worn
one of the four rearmost molars
the folds in the larynx that produce voice
A flat, winglike part of a fish or other aquatic animal used for swimming, steering, or balance.
The outer layer of an organ, especially the outer layer of the brain or kidney.
The male reproductive cell, especially in humans and other animals, capable of fertilizing an egg.
A sharp, curved nail on the end of the toe of an animal or bird, used for gripping, digging, or attacking.
The part of the body between the chest and the pelvis, containing the stomach, intestines, liver, and other internal organs.
The rear section of the body in an arthropod, such as an insect or spider, located behind the thorax and containing many of its internal organs.
An organ or group of cells in an animal that produces and releases substances such as hormones, sweat, saliva, or digestive fluids.
The male reproductive organ used for urination and, in many animals, for sexual reproduction.
A firm, flexible connective tissue that forms parts of the skeleton, covers the ends of bones at joints, and supports structures such as the nose and ears.
The hollow, muscular organ in the female reproductive system where a fertilized egg implants and a fetus develops; the womb.
A female reproductive organ in animals, including humans, that produces eggs and, in many animals, reproductive hormones.
The outermost layer of skin in humans and other animals, forming a protective covering over the body.
A blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart, usually carrying oxygen-rich blood to the body's tissues.
A butterfly-shaped endocrine gland in the front of the neck that produces hormones regulating metabolism, growth, and development.
The middle section of an insect's or other arthropod's body, between the head and abdomen, bearing the legs and, in insects, usually the wings.
The muscular canal in the female reproductive system that extends from the cervix to the outside of the body.
The muscular tube that carries swallowed food and liquid from the throat to the stomach.
An organ that develops in the uterus during pregnancy and connects the fetus to the mother, supplying nutrients and oxygen and removing waste.
A soft organ in the upper left side of the abdomen that filters blood and supports the immune system.
The large bony structure at the base of the spine, formed by the hip bones, sacrum, and coccyx, which supports the trunk and connects it to the legs.
The opening at the end of the digestive tract through which solid waste leaves the body.
A strong band of fibrous connective tissue that connects bones at a joint and helps hold them together.
The thin layer of dead skin at the base and sides of a fingernail or toenail.
A hard, crusty deposit that forms on teeth from mineralized dental plaque.
The part of the body on either side of the lower back, between the ribs and the hips.
The surgical removal of the foreskin from the penis, often performed for religious, cultural, medical, or personal reasons.
A hard outer covering of an animal, especially a mollusk, crustacean, egg, or nut.
Hair growing on a person's chin, cheeks, and jaw.
